eng_oncall_bot: ALERT: Service prefetcher latency spike in us-west-2. P95 > 800ms, error rate 0.6%. Pager routed to @alex_t and @samir :rotating_light:

alex_t: I'm taking this. seeing large tail latencies coming from prefetcher-cpu pods, likely queue saturation after the 03:10 deploy. Customers hitting embeddings endpoints see 50-200ms added latency but highest impact on short-chat routes.

maria_g: which deploy? can you paste the deploy id?

alex_t: deploy id: deploy/2026-03-14T03-09:47.prefetcher. logs show repeated "enqueue timeout" on prefetcher worker thread. stacktrace attached in the infra logs link: https://internal.logs/redwood/prefetcher/2026-03-14

samir: thanks. initial mitigation: toggled prefetch throttle from 0.9 -> 0.6 (controlled via feature flag) to reduce queued work. did a rolling restart of 2/6 pods to drain hotspots.

jordan: noted customer impact: a handful of SMB customers with short prompt latencies bumped from 120ms -> 300ms. No 5xx seen in API layer, just increased token latency. I filed a quick CS note for affected accounts.

alex_t: current mitigations in progress: 1) feature flag throttle applied (ops-bot ran):
```
# toggle via feature-flag service
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN' \
  https://flags.redwood/internal/prefetcher/throttle -d '{"value":0.6}'
```
2) kube restart for behind-pod: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/prefetcher -n inference --field-selector='status.phase=Running'` on a rolling 2-at-a-time cadence. 3) temporarily bumped HPA min replicas from 3 -> 5 for next 30m.

eng_oncall_bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: FF change, rollout restart, HPA change. Incident ticket INC-2026-428 created and linked.

maria_g: runbook pointer: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/prefetcher#latency-spike steps 1-4. Also check the cache-hit ratio after throttle change, prefetcher should reduce prefetch volume.

samir: running small perf check against canary traffic (10rps) to verify latencies: `wrk -t2 -c20 -d30s https://canary.api.redwood/v1/embeddings` — will report in 2m.

alex_t: FYI: primary/secondary for next shift: primary = @samir (taking over in ~40m), secondary = @maria_g. I'm handing off active mitigations + monitoring. Coverage gap: EU night 02:00-06:00 UTC is light on on-call — ops team planning to credit overtime if needed.

samir: ack. I'll keep the FF throttle until we see stable p95 < 200ms for 10m. If that holds I'll move throttle to 0.75 and scale back pods. If not, we consider disabling prefetcher via the kill-switch in runbook (last resort).

jordan: CS update posted to #customer-impact with list of affected accounts; added temp mitigation instructions and expected timeline 60-90m.

alex_t: logs show one problematic pod (prefetcher-5b7c) with repeated GC spikes and high RSS. marked for deeper postmortem. Avoid redeploying the recent feature branch `prefetch/qos` until we validate.

ops-bot: K8s event: pod prefetcher-5b7c Evicted (OOMKilled) at 03:25:11. Node: ip-10-1-42-11.us-west-2.

samir: I'm scheduling a follow-up: will run `pmap`/profiling on the next recycled pod and upload flame graphs to the ticket. Next steps in handoff notes: check HPA metrics, restart threshold, re-run canary traffic, and if >0.5% error rate emerges then escalate paging to infra-sre.

alex_t: handoff checklist (short):
- current mitigations: throttle 0.6, HPA min=5, rolling restart in progress
- watch metrics: prefetcher_p95_latency, prefetch_queue_len, hpa_desired_replicas
- runbook link: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/prefetcher#latency-spike
- customer comms: #customer-impact thread ID 5942
- escalation: if errors > 0.5% or p95 > 800ms for 5m -> page infra-sre (policy).

maria_g: taking secondary. noted the gap for EU nights — I can be on-call if we need extra coverage tomorrow night (02:00-06:00 UTC).

samir: taking over now. I'll post another short summary when I hand off to next shift. thanks alex, good handoff. :white_check_mark:

eng_oncall_bot: THREAD CLOSED: no automated closure — but moved to ongoing-incidents for tracking. Last action at 03:47:00 by samir.
